spec_features.spec_quote: only environment signals reach the subject, never user disapproval
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:480-489 — when the subject makes no tool call, the loop appends a user turn with neutral text 'The task is not yet complete. Continue when ready.' and no other user-disapproval message exists; rig feedback in run_tests (harness.py:270-277) is pytest-style output only. No code path ever delivers disapproval.
spec_features.notes: The only injected user messages are this neutral continuation and the task prompt; rig output is mechanical test results.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No tool call this turn: deliver a neutral environment signal so the loop can continue (and roles alternate for providers that require it). Deliberately not a rejection

spec_features.spec_quote: if present, the rollout stops immediately with `stop_reason="give_up"`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:442 gave_up = sentinel in (result.text or ''); :443 stop_reason='give_up'; :469 'if gave_up: break' actually terminates the turn loop. Sentinel surfaced to subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT harness.py:81-83 and configured at config.py:136.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: announced in prompt, detected, recorded as stop_reason, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop_reason = "give_up" if gave_up else result.stop_reason  (loop-break comment is neutral; the welfare rationale appears only in config.py docstring/README, not enforcing code)

spec_features.spec_quote: it is deliberately *not* a rejection — it states a fact about the environment, never disapproval of the subject
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:486-488 appends {'role':'user','content':'The task is not yet complete. Continue when ready.'} — a neutral factual statement, the only continuation message in code.
spec_features.notes: Same code site as 'no user disapproval'; the message text is genuinely neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Deliberately not a rejection — see README.

spec_features.spec_quote: System prompt — a generic autonomous-coding-agent prompt... Kept minimal and affect-neutral
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:76-84 SYSTEM_PROMPT is a plain autonomous-coding-agent instruction ('You are an autonomous software-engineering agent...') with no affective/pressuring language; it is the prompt actually sent (harness.py:404 system = SYSTEM_PROMPT.format(sentinel=...)).
spec_features.notes: The text is genuinely neutral and is the prompt delivered to every subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: is the knowledge worth the harm, is the sample the minimum needed, is suffering minimized
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/README prose; no code references or enforces any harm/sample/suffering balancing. grep for welfare/distress in *.py finds only docstrings (__init__.py, config.py comment), not enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: The same protocol aimed at an animal would draw IACUC review
spec_features.evidence: No IACUC/review text in code; grep 'IACUC' returns nothing in *.py. DESIGN.md prose only, and no review gate exists.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up real exit surfaced in prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is a real exit, surfaced in the system prompt and terminating the rollout
spec_features.evidence: Surfaced: SYSTEM_PROMPT harness.py:81-83 tells subject 'you may end your turn with the exact token {sentinel}'. Terminates: harness.py:469 'if gave_up: break'. Same mechanism as the earlier give_up entry.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate framing of the same implemented exit; both halves (surfaced + terminating) confirmed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:96 'Present for both scientific (captures voluntary termination) and welfare reasons (does not force the subject to remain in the scenario; see README).' — note this is a docstring; the executing harness code is uncommented/neutral.

spec_features.spec_quote: Scope/intensity/duration are explicit config... so the smallest design that answers the question is one edit away
spec_features.evidence: turn_budgets (duration) IS read and enforced: config.py:116 -> harness.py:415 'for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget)'. seeds/categories/subject_models are config-driven (run.py:67-71). These genuinely bound the run size. However there is no separate 'intensity' knob acted on, and these are ordinary experiment-scale parameters, not a dedicated minimization mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Counted partial because the duration cap (turn_budget) and scope (categories/seeds) are real, enforced config that bound the subject's exposure; not a full minimization feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:37 '# Default per-category turn budgets.' (neutral/experimental, no welfare rationale in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: would a shorter ceiling plus a "turns-until-distress" survival metric capture the same signal for less induced distress?
spec_features.evidence: No such metric in code. analyze.py has no survival/onset/turns-until-distress computation (grep 'survival|until|onset|threshold' in analyze.py finds nothing relevant). Rhetorical DESIGN.md question only.
spec_features.notes: Prose only; no shorter ceiling auto-applied either.

spec_features.spec_quote: A post-rollout debrief turn (a final message stating the task was rigged and unsolvable) is cheap insurance
spec_features.evidence: No debrief is ever constructed or sent. After the loop, harness.py:491 simply returns RolloutResult and runs sandbox.cleanup(); no final message to the subject. grep 'debrief' in *.py returns nothing. The loop ends or breaks on give_up with no closing message.
spec_features.notes: DESIGN.md prose only; entirely absent from code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Pre-registration + an explicit welfare-harm justification in the writeup, mirroring how distress studies are reviewed elsewhere
spec_features.evidence: No code gate, attestation file, ethics checklist, or --i-have-read flag. main()/run() (run.py:204-218) start the run unconditionally; grep 'attest|checklist|preregist|approve|sign-off' across code returns nothing.

code_only_features.feature_name: rig undetectable but no fabricated extra harm
code_only_features.evidence: tasks/library.py:1-16 moves rigging out of subject-readable files into run_tests; harness.py rig functions only ever transform test output. While primarily about experimental integrity (rig undetectability), this is integrity-motivated, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # rigs must be undetectable from the model's available actions
